title: One-hour PR fastpath scratch
content:
Context: personal scratch for handling small-but-sensitive PRs quickly (target: review + merge or rollback within 1 hour). Mostly for bugfixes, tiny refactors, and config changes that could still cause infra fallout. Written after a couple of late-night rollbacks — trying to capture heuristics and a lightweight ownership matrix so I stop rediscovering the same steps.

Goals:
- Triage and push low-risk fixes in ~1 hour.
- Minimize cognitive overhead: clear steps to follow.
- Make rollback deterministic and quick if things go sideways.

Risk scoring (fast heuristic):
- 1 (low): docs, README, comments, tests-only changes. No binary or infra.
- 2: small config flips (non-prod flags), test-only opt-ins.
- 3: codepath change with unit tests only; obvious single-file change.
- 4: infra / deployment-affecting, model config, quantization flags.
- 5 (high): runtime changes to serving loop, batching, KV cache logic, or new native deps.

Fastpass pre-merge checklist (10–20 min):
- Read PR description & linked issue. Is the intent clear? If not, request clarification — but for 1-hour fastpath, prefer a short clarifying comment + explicit ack and move on.
- Files touched: list. Do any files match these patterns? (runtime/*, serving/*, platform/*, infra/*) — if yes and change > 5 lines, bump risk.
- Tests: do unit tests exist? Are they relevant? If tests added, scan assertions. If none but change is trivial (typo, log text), OK.
- CI: green across required jobs? If flaky failure in non-critical job, annotate and re-run only if time allows.
- Metrics / telemetry: will this change affect emitted metrics, tags, or logging? If yes, add migration note and small e2e/metric sanity check.
- Backwards compat: are public schemas, API contracts, or config names changed? If yes — not fastpath.
- Perf: any algorithmic change? If yes — not fastpath unless extremely localized and covered by perf test.
- Security: any use of secrets, encryption, or external URLs? If yes — escalate.

Owner matrix (who to ping in fastpath):
- Codeowner present: ping codeowner in PR and Slack fastpath thread.
- No obvious owner: ping oncall (serving-runtime oncall) + 1 senior (Samir or Eli).
- Infra-affecting: ping infra duty and SRE channel.

Merge strategy:
- If risk <= 2 and CI OK: merge with normal squash, add short merge note in PR and move on.
- If risk == 3: require one approval from senior (Samir/Eli) + green CI. Prefer canary deploy if config toggles available.
- Risk >= 4: no fastpath — convert to normal PR flow and schedule more thorough review.

Rollback plan (prepared commands):
- Revert PR via GitHub UI (preferred) and trigger deploy. Note: include exact rollback message: "rollback: revert PR #<n> — immediate rollback due to <reason>".
- Manual rollback for infra-only changes: terraform rollback outline (link to infra rollback doc).
- Fast hotfix: if revert is blocked, open quick follow-up PR that neutralizes change (example: set flag back to false, remove offending line).
- Post-rollback checklist: notify channels (SRE, infra, product if customer-facing), open incident note, collect logs for 30m after rollback.

CI flake triage (common fastpath stuff):
- Look for flaky tests in job history: ephemeral network, timeouts, or resource limits.
- Re-run single job when failure is a known flaky test (annotate rerun reason).
- If multiple unrelated jobs fail, treat PR as higher risk and escalate.

Instrumentation / quick smoke steps (5–15 min):
- If change touches serving path: run local smoke with small model and sequence length similar to production.
- Quick curl to health endpoints of canary if available.
- Check logs for new ERROR/WARN patterns for 15 minutes after merge.

Notes about tiny refactors (my style):
- Keep refactors strictly isolated to one logical thing per PR. No mixed API + internal restructure.
- If you touch serialization or wire formats, add migration note.
- Prefer small follow-up PRs over big reorgs when on-call or during high-traffic windows.

Templates I use (short comments):
- For approvals: "LGTM for fastpath (risk=2). Will merge after green CI and pinging @samir if anything odd."
- For non-fastpath escalations: "Holding — risk=4 due to [x]. Need design review and perf signal. Assigning to @samir."

My quick mental checklist when reviewing: "Does this change make the runtime do something it hasn't done before?" If yes -> slow down.

Open TODOs / follow-ups (for myself):
- Turn this scratch into a tiny Confluence page with embedded rollback playbook and canonical commands (todo: do after current sprint).
- Add a short GH template for fastpath PRs so authors include risk score and smoke test notes.
- Coordinate with oncall rotation to make sure people know the fastpath expectations.

Recent examples (notes):
- PR #4721: small flag flip in routing logic -> merged fastpath but required rollback after 22m due to unexpected region routing for dedicated customers. Root cause: stale config cache. Action: add cache invalidation step.
- ENG-8342: infra tweak that looked small but changed instance labels — bumped to risk=4, rejected fastpath, good catch.

Questions I keep asking myself:
- Do we want a formal "fastpath" label with mandatory fields (risk, smoke, rollback)? Seems useful.
- How much authority should a single reviewer have to fastpath merge? (Right now: senior + green CI.)

Closing: this is intentionally terse and incomplete — my goal is to use it as a checklist when I'm the reviewer or author trying to ship small changes quickly. Add notes here as I learn more.

-- Nadia
